editorial.headline: Machine Tools for Metal and Other Hard Materials
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28220 covers the manufacture of industrial machine tools, nationally open to foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28220 is a manufacturing code for the machinery behind industrial fabrication: machine tools used to make or work metal and other hard materials such as wood, bone, stone, hard plastic, hard rubber and cold glass. Its scope is not limited to conventional cutting or forming equipment. The record includes machine tools using laser beams, electromagnetic waves, plasma sparks, magnetic vibration and similar technologies, placing this activity squarely in the industrial-production layer rather than in general trading or light workshop services.

The activity reaches across a broad workshop floor. It includes machines for turning, drilling, milling, forming, planing, grinding, pressing and stamping. It also covers punch presses, hydraulic presses, hydraulic brakes, hammers, forging machines, draw-benches, thread rollers and machinery for working cable. Stationary machines for nailing, stapling, gluing or assembling wood, cork, bone, hard rubber and plastic are within scope, as are drilling, filling, riveting and sheet-metal cutting machines. The record also includes particle-board pressing machines, electroplating machines, and parts or accessories integrated into machine tools, including work holders, dividing heads and other specialised components.

This is therefore a serious industrial-manufacturing registration, not merely a label for portable tools or consumables. The record expressly leaves out interchangeable tools for hand tools or machine tools, hand electric soldering equipment, and powered hand tools. For applicants, that distinction matters because the centre of gravity here is the manufacture of machine tools themselves and the specialised parts that become part of those machines. The code is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the record does not confine it to one enterprise size.

Nationally, the investment signal is clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the national source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali is the hard stop. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, and the record says: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". The moratorium rule is also explicit: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. The honest reading is that a foreign investor can treat this code as nationally open, but cannot register it as PMA in Bali under the Bali-side block recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally the code is open to 100% foreign ownership, but Bali is the hard stop for PMA registration under the recorded moratorium.
